title: Uncovering Real GPU NoC Characteristics: Implications on Interconnect Architecture
problem: Real GPU NoCs exhibit non-uniform on-chip latency of up to 70% difference between cores and memory partitions based on physical location, while multi-partition GPUs show varying interconnect characteristics. This non-uniformity is not well understood and has implications for system design and security.
motivation: Understanding real GPU NoC characteristics is critical for designing efficient interconnects that avoid bottlenecks, correctly modeling timing-based side-channel attacks, and making proper microarchitecture assumptions.
method: The paper performs detailed empirical analysis of GPU NoCs across multiple NVIDIA GPU generations, measuring latency and bandwidth between cores and memory partitions. They characterize non-uniform latency based on physical location and analyze multi-partition GPU interconnect behavior, then demonstrate how this non-uniformity can be exploited in timing side-channel attacks.
key_novelty: First comprehensive empirical characterization of non-uniform latency in real GPU NoCs across modern NVIDIA generations and demonstration of its exploitability in timing side-channel attacks.
contributions: Detailed empirical analysis of GPU NoC latency and bandwidth characteristics across multiple NVIDIA GPU generations
Discovery and quantification of non-uniform on-chip latency (up to 70%) based on core physical location
Characterization of interconnect behavior in multi-partition GPU architectures
Demonstration of timing side-channel attack exploiting NoC non-uniformity
Design implications for GPU interconnect microarchitectures

metrics.other: latency non-uniformity (up to 70%), bandwidth characteristics across core-memory partition pairs

limitations: Analysis is limited to NVIDIA GPUs; applicability to other GPU vendors and detailed quantitative implications for specific applications are not discussed.
primary_theme: GPU interconnect non-uniformity characterization and security implications
